title: Planning a retreat you sell
lead: Every task for an open training retreat that you design, market and fill with individual bookings, rather than run for one client. You carry the risk, so selling and the go or no-go decision get as much care as the design.

phases.name: Set up once
phases.when: Before your first retreat, then review each year
phases.note: Not repeated every time. Do these once and keep them up to date.

phases.name: Sell
phases.when: From launch until it is full
phases.note: Selling runs alongside design and preparation. Review sales at fixed points, not every day.

phases.name: Arrive and set up
phases.when: The day before, and the first morning

tasks.title: Arrange business insurance
tasks.why: Venues, clients and activity providers will ask for it.
steps: Public liability cover
Professional indemnity cover
Check outdoor and movement activities are covered
Note the renewal date in your calendar
tasks.done: Certificates saved, and the cover matches every kind of activity you run.

tasks.title: Write your booking terms
tasks.why: Selling to the public brings consumer law into play.
steps: Payment schedule: deposit and balance date
Cancellation and refunds, by you and by the guest
Transfers to another date or another person
What happens if numbers are too low
Check consumer law on cancellation rights with a legal professional, especially for bookings made online
tasks.done: A legal professional has reviewed them and they are on the booking page.

tasks.title: Set up bookings and payments
tasks.why: People should be able to book and pay in one go.
steps: A booking page with dates, price and what is included
Card payments, deposits and balance reminders
A booking form that collects only what you need
Automatic confirmation emails
tasks.done: You have made a test booking from start to finish.

tasks.title: Build a mailing list with consent
tasks.why: Your past guests and interested people are your cheapest sales.
steps: A sign-up form with clear consent to marketing emails
Only email people who have opted in
An easy way to unsubscribe
tasks.done: The sign-up works and every contact has given consent.

tasks.title: Build your retreat templates
tasks.why: Copying a ready folder and board saves a day on every retreat.
steps: Google Drive folder with the seven numbered folders used on this page
Notion board with these cards
Templates for the brief, budget, attendee list, run sheet and incident log
tasks.done: You can set up a new retreat in under five minutes.

tasks.title: Build your supplier list
tasks.why: Vetted venues and suppliers you can call on quickly.
steps: Venues you have visited, with notes
Transport, catering extras, activity providers, photographers
Associates and facilitators you trust
Insurance and qualifications checked for each
tasks.done: At least two options in each category, each checked.

tasks.title: Define who it is for
tasks.why: A retreat for everyone sells to no one.
steps: The people it is for, and the problem it helps with
Who it is not for
Where those people already gather and listen
tasks.done: You can describe the ideal guest in two sentences.

tasks.title: Write the promise
tasks.why: What people will do and leave with, stated honestly.
steps: What happens, where, with whom and for how long
What people leave with
Promise the conditions, never a transformation
tasks.done: A friend in the target audience can repeat it back accurately.

tasks.title: Test demand before you commit
tasks.why: Find out whether people will pay before you sign a venue.
steps: Talk to eight to ten people in the audience
Share the idea with your mailing list and count replies
Open a waiting list or take refundable deposits
Set a number that tells you to go ahead
tasks.done: You have the number you set, or have decided to change the offer.

tasks.title: Choose format, length and season
tasks.why: These decide the venue search and the budget.
steps: Residential or day-based, and how many nights
What sits before and after the event
Season, daylight and weather
Clashes: school holidays, year end, religious festivals
Travel: a place most people can reach by train
tasks.done: You have chosen a format and two possible date windows.

tasks.title: Set capacity and minimum numbers
tasks.why: Know the most you can hold and the fewest you can run with.
steps: Maximum for the venue and the design
Minimum to break even
Minimum to run well as a group
The date by which you decide
tasks.done: Maximum, minimum and the decision date are written down.

tasks.title: Build the budget and break-even
tasks.why: Price it so it pays even if it does not sell out.
steps: Fixed costs: venue hire, facilitators, marketing
Costs per guest: rooms, food, materials
Booking platform and card payment fees
Contingency
Your margin
Break-even number of guests
tasks.done: You know how many guests you need to break even and to make your margin.

tasks.title: Set prices and ticket types
tasks.why: Price for the people you want, and make it simple.
steps: Check what similar retreats charge and include
Full price, and an early-bird price with an end date
Room types, such as shared or single
Show prices to the public including VAT
Any places offered at a lower price, and how you choose who gets them
tasks.done: Prices are set, include VAT, and still beat break-even.

tasks.title: Decide to go ahead
tasks.why: Commit only when the demand test and the numbers both say yes.
steps: Demand test met
Break-even is realistic
You have the time to sell it
tasks.done: Decision written down, with the reason.

tasks.title: Set up the project
tasks.why: One place for everything, shared with your team.
steps: Copy the folder and board templates
Share with the team
List who does what
tasks.done: The board is set up and the team has access.

tasks.title: Shortlist and visit venues
tasks.why: See the rooms at the time of day you will use them.
steps: Score venues on rooms, outdoor space, access, food, quiet, bedrooms and travel
Shortlist three
Visit, and photograph every space
Check step-free routes, fire exits and a wet-weather space
Ask for their risk assessment and insurance
tasks.done: You have chosen a venue.

tasks.title: Contract the venue
tasks.why: Without a client, you carry the venue risk yourself.
steps: You sign, so you carry the risk
Negotiate release dates for unsold rooms
Minimum numbers and the final-numbers deadline
Cancellation dates and charges
Damage and extra charges
tasks.done: Contract signed, deposit paid, and every deadline added to the tracker.

tasks.title: Book the facilitation team
tasks.why: Book people early. Good facilitators fill their diaries.
steps: Lead and second facilitator
Anyone for wellbeing, movement or outdoor sessions
Check qualifications and insurance
Send each a short contract
tasks.done: Everyone has confirmed in writing.

tasks.title: Line up a backup facilitator
tasks.why: If you or your lead falls ill, the retreat still runs.
steps: Name someone who could step in at short notice
Agree a fee for standby and for stepping in
Share the plans two weeks before
tasks.done: A named backup has agreed in writing and has the plans.

tasks.title: Book other suppliers
tasks.why: Transport, activities and extras.
steps: Coach or minibus transfers
Outdoor or activity providers
Photographer, speakers or musicians
Check insurance, qualifications and risk assessments for each
tasks.done: Every supplier has confirmed in writing, with documents saved.

tasks.title: Confirm the insurance covers this retreat
tasks.why: Each retreat may add activities or places your cover does not include.
steps: Activities, outdoor sessions and venue
Anything abroad
Ask your broker if unsure
tasks.done: You have confirmed cover for every activity on this retreat.

tasks.title: Check the VAT on prices and costs
tasks.why: VAT changes what guests pay and what you keep.
steps: Check whether you need to be VAT registered: see the current threshold on GOV.UK
Show prices with and without VAT in the proposal
Check whether venue and supplier quotes include VAT
If you are registered, keep VAT invoices so you can reclaim
For anything abroad, check the VAT rules there with an accountant
tasks.deliverable: VAT notes in the costing sheet
tasks.done: Every price and cost in the costing sheet says whether it includes VAT.

tasks.title: Plan the personal data
tasks.why: Decide what you collect before you collect it.
steps: What you need and why
Who can see it
Where it is kept (the restricted folder)
When it will be deleted
A short privacy note for attendees
tasks.done: The note is written and the deletion date is in the tracker.

tasks.title: Draft the programme outline
tasks.why: The booking page has to describe days you have not designed in detail yet.
steps: The shape of each day
The key sessions and what each is for
What is included, and what is not
Who will facilitate
General enough to refine, specific enough to be honest
tasks.done: The outline is on the booking page, and the detailed design starts from it.

tasks.title: Build the booking page
tasks.why: Everything a guest needs to decide and book.
steps: The promise, who it is for and who it is not for
Dates, place, price and what is included
The outline of each day
Access, food and rooms
Venue photos you have permission to use, and facilitator bios
Booking terms and a privacy note
A clear way to ask a question
tasks.done: Live, tested on a phone, and a test booking has gone through.

tasks.title: Plan the marketing
tasks.why: Decide where the guests will come from before you launch.
steps: Your mailing list and past guests
Social media and content
Partners who reach the same people
Referrals from past guests
A weekly sales target to the full date
tasks.done: Each channel has an owner and a weekly target.

tasks.title: Agree the sales checkpoints
tasks.why: Fixed dates to check sales, so you act in time.
steps: Launch
Early-bird end
Twelve, eight and six weeks before
The minimum-numbers decision date
What you will do at each if sales are behind
tasks.done: Each checkpoint has a date and a target.

tasks.title: Launch to your list first
tasks.why: The people who already know you book first.
steps: Email the waiting list and past guests before anyone else
Give them early access or the early-bird price
Then launch publicly
tasks.done: Launch emails sent, and first bookings recorded.

tasks.title: Run the marketing
tasks.why: Steady, honest promotion until the retreat is full.
steps: Post and send to the plan
Answer every enquiry within a day
Share stories and testimonials only with consent
Avoid claims you cannot support, especially about the brain or health
tasks.done: Every planned piece has gone out, and enquiries are answered.

tasks.title: Review sales at each checkpoint
tasks.why: Act early if sales are behind.
steps: Bookings against the target
Which channels are working
Adjust: more promotion, partners, or a change of date
Release unsold rooms by the venue's date
tasks.done: Each checkpoint has a written decision.

tasks.title: Collect balances and manage changes
tasks.why: Money and changes need tracking as bookings come in.
steps: Send balance reminders before the due date
Handle cancellations and transfers to your terms
Keep a waiting list if it sells out
tasks.done: All balances paid by the due date, and every change recorded.

tasks.title: Design the before, during and after
tasks.why: The retreat is the middle of a programme, not the whole of it.
steps: A welcome email and any pre-work
A short call or video for each guest beforehand, if it helps
The follow-up sessions and reminders after, with dates
tasks.done: Every part has a date and an owner.

tasks.title: Draft the timetable
tasks.why: The shape of the days decides how much people take in.
steps: Hardest work when energy is highest
Real breaks and solo time
Low-risk activities before anything personal
An indoor version of every outdoor slot
Nothing intense after dinner, and a clear end each day
Absorption over intensity: fewer, deeper sessions
tasks.done: The timetable is final and matches what the booking page promised.

tasks.title: Write the session plans
tasks.why: A plan for every slot means anyone on the team could run it.
steps: Objective
Method and timings
Materials
Facilitator notes
What to cut if time runs short
tasks.done: Every slot in the timetable has a plan.

tasks.title: Test the riskiest activities
tasks.why: An activity that has never been run is the one most likely to fail.
steps: Pick the activities that are new, physical or emotionally demanding
Try them with colleagues or a few attendees
Fix the timings and the instructions
tasks.done: Each new or risky activity has been tried once.

tasks.title: Plan outdoor, movement and reflection time
tasks.why: Use the setting on purpose.
steps: Outdoor sessions with a reason, and a wet-weather plan
Optional movement at different levels
Solo time with a prompt
tasks.done: Each has a purpose, a slot and a fallback.

tasks.title: Plan the evenings
tasks.why: Evenings shape the mood and the risks.
steps: Optional, with a clear end time for anything organised
A good alcohol-free offer
Something other than the bar: food, a fire, a walk, a game
tasks.done: The rules are set and are in the joining instructions.

tasks.title: Set phone and work-contact rules
tasks.why: Clear rules help guests switch off.
steps: When people can check in with work
How urgent contact reaches them
Say it in advance
tasks.done: The rules are in the joining instructions.

tasks.title: Design for everyone
tasks.why: Check the design works for the whole group, not the typical person.
steps: A version for people who cannot stay overnight
Access needs in rooms, routes and activities
Different minds: quiet space, clear instructions, choice
Faith, dietary and caring needs
Accessible materials: readable type, captions
tasks.done: Each known need has an answer in the plan.

tasks.title: Plan the groups and rooms
tasks.why: Who sits and works with whom changes what people learn.
steps: Small groups and pairs that mix people
Match guests who booked shared rooms, and ask before you pair anyone
Single rooms for anyone who booked one
tasks.done: Lists are ready for the run sheet and the venue.

tasks.title: Plan the feedback and testimonials
tasks.why: You need honest feedback, and stories you are allowed to use.
steps: A short feedback form for the last session
A separate question asking permission to quote
A follow-up question at thirty days on what changed
tasks.done: Forms are built and tested.

tasks.title: Make the materials
tasks.why: Everything people see, hold or take away.
steps: Slides and handouts
Workbook or cards
Flipcharts drawn in advance
Name badges and signs
Proofread everything
tasks.done: Everything is proofread and on the print list.

tasks.title: Run a pre-mortem
tasks.why: Imagine it went badly, and fix the likely causes now.
steps: List why it might go badly
Pick the three most likely
Change the design or add a plan for each
tasks.done: The top three risks each have a response.

tasks.title: Rehearse the hard sessions
tasks.why: Timings and hand-overs go wrong when untested.
steps: Run the trickiest sessions with the team
Check timings
Agree who does what
tasks.done: The team has run through every session that is new or high-stakes.

tasks.title: Write the duty-of-care plan
tasks.why: Guests come without an employer behind them, so your duty of care matters even more.
steps: What people are told in advance
Consent and the right to opt out
The limits of your role
Signs someone needs support
Who to call, and who is in charge
tasks.done: The team has read it, and guests have been told what they need to know.

tasks.title: Send the guest questionnaire
tasks.why: One form for everything, so guests are not asked twice.
steps: What they hope to get from the retreat
Travel and arrival
Dietary needs, including severe allergies
Access needs
Emergency contact
The health questions the activities need
Photo consent
Chase anyone who has not replied
tasks.done: Every guest has replied.

tasks.title: Check guests are suited to it
tasks.why: Some activities are not right for everyone.
steps: Describe the physical and emotional demands honestly on the booking page
Read every answer to the health questions
Talk to anyone whose answers raise a question
Offer an alternative or a refund if it is not right for them
tasks.done: Every guest has answered, and any concerns are resolved.

tasks.title: Complete the risk assessment
tasks.why: Covers every activity, the venue, travel and the outdoors.
steps: Hazards, who could be harmed and how
What you will do about each
Check suppliers' own assessments
Review whenever anything changes
tasks.done: Done, signed, and reviewed since the last change.

tasks.title: Write the incident plan
tasks.why: Everyone knows what to do when something goes wrong.
steps: Who is in charge
First aider, nearest hospital and pharmacy
Each guest's emergency contact
The incident log
tasks.done: Every team member knows their role in it.

tasks.title: Plan for severe allergies
tasks.why: A serious allergic reaction is a real emergency risk at any event with food.
steps: Ask about severe allergies separately from dietary preferences, including whether people carry an adrenaline auto-injector
Send the venue kitchen a named list and get written confirmation of how they will handle it
Check the menus and how food will be labelled
Brief the first aider and the team on who is at risk and where auto-injectors are kept
Check activity snacks and evening food too, not only meals
tasks.done: The venue has confirmed in writing, and the team knows who is at risk.

tasks.title: Send the joining instructions
tasks.why: People arrive calmer when they know what to expect.
steps: Purpose and an outline of the days
Travel and arrival times
What to bring, including for the weather
Phones, evenings and alcohol
Access, and who to contact
Describe it honestly: promise the conditions, not a transformation
tasks.done: Sent to every attendee.

tasks.title: Brief the team and suppliers
tasks.why: Everyone you bring in shares the purpose and the rules.
steps: Purpose and the group
The timetable and their part
The rules, the duty-of-care plan and the incident plan
tasks.done: Each person has confirmed they have read it.

tasks.title: Arrange travel and transfers
tasks.why: Travel is where most things go wrong on the day.
steps: Train times and connections
Pick-ups and parking
Travel for the team and kit
A plan for late arrivals
tasks.done: Everyone knows how they are getting there.

tasks.title: Hold the go/no-go check
tasks.why: Decide on numbers by the date you set, while refunds and venue terms still allow it.
steps: Bookings against the minimum
Weather and travel disruption
Every supplier and team member confirmed
If you cancel: refund everyone to your terms and tell them personally
tasks.done: Decision written down and, if cancelling, every guest told and refunded.

tasks.title: Confirm final numbers with the venue
tasks.why: The contract sets a deadline. Miss it and you pay for empty places.
steps: Final numbers
Rooming list
Dietary and access list
tasks.done: The venue has confirmed them in writing before the deadline.

tasks.title: Send the venue the full brief
tasks.why: The venue team can only deliver what they know about.
steps: Room layouts and timings
Meals and dietary list
Kit and technology
A quiet room
Quiet hours and signs
tasks.done: The venue lead has confirmed it.

tasks.title: Write the run sheet
tasks.why: Minute by minute, so nobody has to ask.
steps: Each slot: time, what, who, where, kit
Share it with the team and the venue
tasks.done: The team and the venue have the final version.

tasks.title: Hold the team briefing
tasks.why: Walk through the days together before you arrive.
steps: The run sheet and roles
The duty-of-care and incident plans
Two or three "what if" scenarios
Who is on call out of hours
tasks.done: Everyone has attended or watched the recording.

tasks.title: Print and pack
tasks.why: Pack against a list, not from memory.
steps: Materials, badges and signs
Run sheets, contact sheet and incident log
Pens, flipchart paper, tape, extension leads, speaker
Weather kit and a spare first aid kit
tasks.done: Every item on the kit list is ticked.

tasks.title: Send the final reminder
tasks.why: A week before: the details people forget.
steps: Arrival time and travel
Weather and what to bring
Who to contact on the day
tasks.done: Sent to every attendee.

tasks.title: Check the weather plan
tasks.why: Decide early which outdoor sessions move inside.
steps: Check the forecast
Switch to indoor versions where needed
Tell people what to bring
tasks.done: The run sheet shows which version of each outdoor slot you will run.

tasks.title: Walk the venue
tasks.why: Know the building before the group does.
steps: Every room and outdoor space
Fire exits and assembly point
Toilets and step-free routes
The quiet room
tasks.done: You could guide someone to any space and out in an emergency.

tasks.title: Meet the venue lead
tasks.why: One conversation saves many on the day.
steps: Timings and meals
The dietary list
Fire alarm tests
Who to call, day and night
tasks.done: You have the venue lead's number and they have the run sheet.

tasks.title: Set up the rooms and technology
tasks.why: Set up the night before if you can.
steps: Furniture, walls and materials
Signs and the quiet room
Screen, sound and wifi tested
A plan that needs no technology
tasks.done: The first session could start now.

tasks.title: Set up the welcome
tasks.why: The first ten minutes set the tone.
steps: Welcome desk, badges and room keys
First aider identified
Incident log and contact sheet in place
tasks.done: Ready before the first person arrives.

tasks.title: Open the retreat
tasks.why: Mark the start, and give people what they need to settle.
steps: Welcome and purpose, with a short welcome from the sponsor if they can
Housekeeping: exits, alarms, toilets, wifi
Phones, evenings and photo consent
How you will work together
What people will leave with
tasks.done: Everyone knows the purpose, the rules and where things are.

tasks.title: Run the daily check-ins
tasks.why: Small adjustments each day keep the retreat on track.
steps: Team, morning and evening: energy, concerns, changes
Venue: meal numbers and changes
Cut or move sessions rather than run over
tasks.done: Each day ends with an agreed plan for tomorrow.

tasks.title: Capture the outputs every day
tasks.why: Flipcharts get lost and memories fade.
steps: Photograph every flipchart and wall
Record decisions, owners and dates
Upload to the folder each evening
tasks.done: Each day's outputs are in the folder by the end of the evening.

tasks.title: Look after people
tasks.why: Duty of care runs all day and all evening.
steps: Keep the incident log
Check in with anyone struggling
Keep evenings optional
Make sure people leaving early miss nothing that matters
tasks.done: Every incident is logged with what was done.

tasks.title: Close the retreat
tasks.why: Mark the end and send people back with a plan.
steps: Each person writes what they will do in week one
Confirm the follow-up date
Collect the feedback form and quote permission
Tell people about the next date only if they want to hear
tasks.done: Every attendee has a plan and has filled in the form.

tasks.title: Pack down and check out
tasks.why: Leave nothing behind and no surprises on the bill.
steps: Collect materials and lost property
Walk the rooms with the venue for damage
Agree any extra charges before you leave
tasks.done: Rooms are clear and the venue has agreed the final charges.

tasks.title: Send thanks and resources
tasks.why: Their plans and resources, back in their inbox.
steps: Each person's first-use plan
Resources and photos shared with consent
The follow-up date
tasks.done: Sent to every guest.

tasks.title: Debrief the team
tasks.why: Learn while it is fresh.
steps: What worked
What to change
Incidents to follow up
tasks.done: Notes saved with actions.

tasks.title: Read and share the feedback
tasks.why: Find what to keep and what to change.
steps: Summarise the feedback
Pick the quotes you have permission to use
List three changes for next time
tasks.done: Summary written and changes added to the board.

tasks.title: Close any incidents
tasks.why: Nothing left hanging.
steps: Follow up each incident
Update the risk assessment
tasks.done: Every logged incident is closed.

tasks.title: Reconcile costs and profit
tasks.why: Check the venue bill against the contract before you pay.
steps: Check venue and supplier invoices
Pay suppliers and the team
Settle no-shows and any refunds to your terms
Record actual costs and income
Work out the real profit per guest
tasks.done: Everyone paid and the real profit is known.

tasks.title: Ask for reviews
tasks.why: Reviews from real guests sell the next retreat.
steps: Ask happy guests for a review or a short quote
Only use what they have agreed you can use
tasks.done: Reviews requested and permissions recorded.

tasks.title: Send the spaced reminders
tasks.why: A recall question at one and three weeks keeps it alive.
steps: One question to answer from memory
One prompt to use the skill this week
tasks.done: Both reminders sent.

tasks.title: Run the follow-up session
tasks.why: A follow-up call keeps guests connected and the learning alive.
steps: Recall the key ideas
Share what people tried
Solve what got in the way
tasks.done: Session run and notes saved.

tasks.title: Keep guests connected
tasks.why: A light community keeps people learning and brings them back.
steps: A group chat or a quarterly call, if guests want one
Invite past guests to the next retreat first, with consent
tasks.done: Guests have been offered a way to stay in touch.

tasks.title: Gather a case study
tasks.why: Stories of real change sell the next retreat.
steps: Ask one or two guests what changed
Get written consent for how it is used
tasks.done: Written and approved by the people in it.

tasks.title: Delete the personal data
tasks.why: On the date you set at the start.
steps: Booking and health answers
Registration and feedback forms
Photos without consent
Keep marketing consent records
tasks.done: Deleted, and the date recorded.

tasks.title: Announce the next date
tasks.why: Past guests and the waiting list book first.
steps: Email people who opted in
Offer a returning-guest or referral rate if you use one
tasks.done: Sent to the list.

tasks.title: Run your own retrospective
tasks.why: Improve the templates for next time.
steps: Decide whether to run it again, and what to change
What to change in the offer, price or marketing
What to change in the design
Update this checklist and the templates
tasks.done: The templates and checklist have been updated.

tasks.title: Check you are ready to launch
tasks.why: Launch once, properly, rather than fixing things in front of buyers.
steps: Booking page live and checked on a phone
A test booking and payment, then refunded
Booking terms and privacy note linked
Launch emails and the first posts written
Venue and facilitators confirmed
tasks.done: Every item is checked.
